identification.summary: Microsoft describes POLONIUM (now Plaid Rain) as an operational group based in Lebanon that targeted Israeli organizations, with activity observed since February 2022 [S1]. Microsoft's April 2023 taxonomy update renamed the group Plaid Rain [S1]. Microsoft's June 2022 report counted more than 20 Israeli victims plus one intergovernmental organization with operations in Lebanon [S1]. ESET reported a separate telemetry view showing Israeli targeting since at least September 2021 [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: activity observed since February 2022 [S1]. ESET: Israeli targeting since at least September 2021 [S2][S3].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Plaid Rain (formerly POLONIUM) [S1][S6]. MITRE tracks the group as POLONIUM, G1005 [S5]. The existing record lists INCENDIARY JACKAL as another name per the Microsoft mapping file [S6]. Microsoft found no current links to Volatile Cedar, another Lebanon-linked group [S1].

attribution.sponsor: No government attribution is cited. Microsoft assesses the group is based in Lebanon and coordinates with Iran's Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS)-affiliated actors [S1].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft: high confidence the group is an operational group based in Lebanon; moderate confidence it coordinates with multiple MOIS-affiliated actors [S1].
attribution.basis: Microsoft cites victim overlap and shared tools and techniques: victims previously compromised by MERCURY (MuddyWater), OneDrive C2 use also seen with DEV-0133 (Lyceum), and AirVPN use shared with DEV-0588 (CopyKittens) [S1]. Microsoft raised a possible hand-off model in which MOIS provides access to previously compromised environments, noted as still being verified [S1]. ESET's title and press coverage call the group Iran-affiliated, relying on Microsoft's assessment [S2][S3].

objectives: ESET assesses POLONIUM as interested solely in cyberespionage and reports no wipers, ransomware or other destructive tools [S3]. Microsoft observed theft and exfiltration of data via actor-controlled cloud accounts [S1].

sectors: Law and aviation (downstream of an IT service provider)
regions: Lebanon (one intergovernmental organization with operations there) [S1]
targeting.notes: Microsoft: more than 20 victims, primarily Israeli, focused on critical manufacturing, IT and the defense industry; an Israeli cloud service provider was compromised and used to reach a downstream law firm and an aviation company [S1]. ESET: more than a dozen Israeli organizations across engineering, IT, law, media, insurance and other sectors [S2][S3].

capabilities.summary: Microsoft reports likely initial access via exploitation of Fortinet CVE-2018-13379 (about 80 percent of victims beaconing to graph.microsoft.com ran Fortinet devices; Microsoft says this suggests but does not prove the link), compromise of service providers to reach downstream customers, and use of the plink SSH tool for redundant tunnels [S1]. Custom implants include CreepyDrive (PowerShell; uses an actor-owned OneDrive account for C2 and exfiltration via an embedded OAuth refresh token), CreepySnail (PowerShell backdoor using stolen credentials against actor C2), CreepyBox (MSIL; OneDrive and Dropbox) and others named CreepyRing and CreepyWink [S1]. Microsoft observed malicious multi-tenant OAuth apps with offline_access and Files.ReadWrite.All permissions, and suspended more than 20 malicious OneDrive applications; Microsoft states no OneDrive vulnerability was involved [S1][S3]. ESET counted at least seven custom backdoors since September 2021, five newly named with a Creep suffix, able to log keystrokes, capture screenshots, use the webcam, exfiltrate files and run commands, with C2 over Dropbox, OneDrive and Mega [S2][S3]. ESET reports PapaCreep (discovered September 2022) as the first in C++, using plain TCP command channels [S2][S3].

campaigns.name: Earliest ESET-observed Israeli targeting

campaigns.summary: Microsoft observed POLONIUM activity from February 2022, mainly against Israeli critical manufacturing, IT and defense firms, including a supply-chain compromise of an Israeli cloud service provider.

campaigns.name: Microsoft exposure and OneDrive disruption
campaigns.summary: Microsoft published its analysis, suspended more than 20 malicious OneDrive applications, shipped detections and listed C2 indicators.

campaigns.name: PapaCreep backdoor
campaigns.summary: ESET discovered PapaCreep, a C++ backdoor, as the most recent tool in its reporting; activity was assessed as ongoing.

campaigns.summary: ESET published research on at least seven custom backdoors and the group's use of multiple cloud providers.

campaigns.name: Rename to Plaid Rain
campaigns.summary: Microsoft's taxonomy update renamed POLONIUM to Plaid Rain.

diamond.adversary: Lebanon-based operational group that Microsoft assesses coordinates with MOIS-affiliated actors [S1].
diamond.capability: Custom PowerShell, MSIL and C++ Creep backdoors, plink tunnels, malicious OAuth apps and likely Fortinet CVE-2018-13379 exploitation [S1][S2][S3].
diamond.infrastructure: Actor-owned OneDrive and Dropbox accounts (and Mega per ESET), IPv4 C2 endpoints, plink tunnel endpoints and AirVPN use [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Israeli critical manufacturing, IT, defense, law, aviation, media and insurance organizations, reached in part through a compromised cloud service provider [S1][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Espionage against Israeli organizations, with Microsoft assessing coordination with Iranian MOIS-affiliated actors [S1][S3].
diamond.technology: Internet-facing Fortinet VPN appliances, single-factor VPN accounts, service-provider trust relationships and consumer cloud storage services [S1].

gaps: No cited reporting on activity after ESET's October 2022 publication. Searches for 2023 to 2025 activity returned only 2022 and renaming material; current status is unknown.

Dark Reading's article 'Iran Threatens Israel's Critical Infrastructure With Polonium Proxy' (date not confirmed) reportedly cites an Israel National Cyber Directorate warning of expansion to water and energy and a shift toward destructive attacks. The article could not be opened (fetch blocked), so this is unverified and not used above. It conflicts with ESET's no-destructive-tools observation from 2022 [S3].

Iran link rests on Microsoft's moderate-confidence assessment and a hand-off model Microsoft said was still being verified [S1]. Secondary commentary reportedly notes it is unclear who is behind the group; not independently verified.

ESET's original article, MITRE G1005 page, and CrowdStrike's INCENDIARY JACKAL profile could not be opened directly. ESET content is taken from search summaries and press coverage; CrowdStrike's own description and any other vendor aliases are unverified.
Vendor cluster boundaries: Microsoft's 20-plus victim count and ESET's dozen-plus count come from different telemetry and should not be merged.
Whether the Fortinet CVE-2018-13379 initial-access link is confirmed is unknown; Microsoft calls it suggestive only [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is internet-facing VPN appliances (Fortinet in Microsoft's observations), managed service and cloud service providers with downstream customer access, and tenant OAuth app registration in Microsoft cloud environments [S1]. STEP 2: The group uses legitimate consumer cloud services (OneDrive, Dropbox, Mega) for C2 and exfiltration, so traffic to these services blends with normal use; Microsoft shipped detections and suspended apps in 2022 [S1][S3]. STEP 3: Template is VPN exploitation or provider compromise, then PowerShell or custom backdoor, then cloud-storage C2 and plink tunnels [S1][S3]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued espionage against Israeli and regional defense-industrial and IT targets using Creep-family tooling [S1][S3]. MDCOA, an assessment rather than a sourced finding, is use of a compromised service provider to reach a defense contractor or partner network supporting coalition operations. Candidate indicators: multi-tenant OAuth apps holding only offline_access and Files.ReadWrite.All, workstation beaconing to graph.microsoft.com from unexpected hosts, unexpected plink usage, and single-factor VPN logins [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Microsoft and ESET updates, since sourced activity ends in 2022 and the current status is a gap [S1][S3]. (2) Authorities: OAuth app audits and cloud tenant hunts in partner or contractor environments require coordination with the owning organization and its provider. (3) Mission assurance: enforce MFA on all remote access and audit service provider and partner access [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with allied and partner network defenders; Israeli-focused targeting makes partner reporting the main source of detail.

provenance.importedSummary: POLONIUM is a Lebanon-based group that has primarily targeted Israeli organizations, including critical manufacturing, information technology, and defense industry companies, since at least February 2022. Security researchers assess POLONIUM has coordinated their operations with multiple actors affiliated with Iran’s Ministry of Intelligence and Security (MOIS), based on victim overlap as well as common techniques and tooling.
